title: Where a value comes from - looked at as one with ocoeco's entries and relations (open question 25)
note: A list whose members are only known at runtime (issue #25). 2026-11-13: tried, not only read. A program declared with argenv 0.3.2 cannot take a repeated option with free values, nor more positionals than it names: a list needs a closed set of tokens, and only a list repeats. It is one need with three faces - snapall's --only declared as plain text (October, where this issue came from); an id typed from memory and refused three times in ocoeco's form (this week); and ocoeco's own --gathers, move TABLE ID..., and note --set, which cannot be declared at all. The three options in the issue ask how to permit free values; what the week showed is that the question is where values come from: declared (a closed set), asked (known only at runtime, and the program can tell them), or free (anything). 2026-11-13: designed (decision 2026-11-13-where-a-value-comes-from), prior art recorded (research where-values-come-from). When it lands, snapall's and lab-agent's own completion generators and oco-agent's hand-typed usage retire, and snapall's pinned test turns over: --only becomes a list whose members are asked. 2026-11-13, later the same day: the step designed here is held, not built. Seen from OCO's place (open-commons-observatory/ecosystem, decision 2026-11-13-a-command-line-is-an-entry): what argenv declares is what a lens already declares, and asked is a relation. 2026-11-13, the trial in ocoeco: argenv's reader read a lens entry against records made as the program ran - nothing here had to change. What it showed lacking is not a field: the reader looks one way, taking words in; from a blank, what may enter is not yet answered anywhere but in ocoeco's form, and it needs what only the data knows - which rows exist.
next: the trial in ocoeco: one act declared the way an entry is, read by argenv's reader; what it shows decides what argenv becomes

title: Completions asked as one types: entering made interactive without a terminal view
note: The author, 2026-11-13: argenv can let completions be regenerated on the fly, making the entering of a command itself interactive. What it stands on is already open here: a list whose members are known only at runtime (argenv-open-lists) - the id of an existing row is such a list. 2026-11-13: it is the same need - a value asked of the program is what a shell can offer as one types.
